name: Electro-Industrial & EBM
description: A loop-based, track-oriented club structure driven by a relentless sequenced bassline; includes an alternate vocal-hook variant for more song-oriented crossover cuts.

defaults.concept: Electro-industrial/EBM — a relentless 16th-note sequenced mono-synth bassline that almost never rests, a rigid four-on-the-floor kick, barked/commanding vocals, and clipped military percussion. Built for the dancefloor, not the verse-chorus formula: harmonic movement stays minimal while rhythmic density stays high.

slots.label: Sequencer Warm-Up
slots.purpose: FEEL: Cold anticipation, a machine warming up. TRICK: Let the sequencer run alone for the full section before any percussion enters — establish the loop itself as the song's real subject.
slots.groove: Sequenced 16th-note mono-bassline alone, no kit; rigid and unswung from the first note.

slots.label: The Militant Loop
slots.purpose: FEEL: Militant, physical, unrelenting. PRODUCTION NOTE: Keep the vocal barked and close-mic'd/dry against the wet, reverbed synths, so the voice reads as another mechanical command layer, not a lead performance.
slots.groove: Relentless 16th-note sequenced bassline that never rests, rigid four-on-the-floor kick, clipped metallic percussion accenting the off-beats.

slots.label: The Filtered Strip-Down
slots.purpose: FEEL: Stripped, tense, waiting. TRICK: Cut the kick and bassline out entirely for two bars, leaving only a slow filter-swept pad, before slamming the groove back in on the downbeat.
slots.groove: Kick and bassline drop out; only a filtered pad and sparse metallic clangs remain, tension building via a slow filter sweep.

slots.label: Full-Throttle Climax
slots.purpose: FEEL: Full-throttle, physical climax. PRODUCTION NOTE: Double the sequencer line an octave up as a second interlocking part — this is the 'everybody move' moment the track has been building toward.
slots.groove: Full sequencer returns doubled an octave with a second interlocking 16th-note counter-line; shouted vocal stabs land on the downbeats.

variants.name: Vocal-Hook EBM
variants.description: A more song-oriented crossover form with a distinct chant-along chorus, for EBM that leans toward the dancefloor-pop side of the genre.

slots.label: Sequencer Warm-Up
slots.purpose: FEEL: Cold anticipation, a machine warming up. TRICK: Let the sequencer run alone before any percussion enters.
slots.groove: Sequenced 16th-note mono-bassline alone, no kit; rigid and unswung.

slots.label: The Militant Loop
slots.purpose: FEEL: Militant, physical, unrelenting. PRODUCTION NOTE: Keep the vocal barked and dry against wet, reverbed synths.
slots.groove: Relentless sequenced 16th-note bassline, rigid four-on-the-floor kick, clipped percussion on the off-beats.

slots.label: The Coiling Sweep
slots.purpose: FEEL: Coiling, anticipatory. TRICK: Introduce a rising filter sweep on the pad and a snare roll borrowed from industrial-dance conventions, signaling the hook is about to land.
slots.groove: Rising filter sweep on the pad layered over an accelerating snare roll; the sequencer holds steady underneath.

slots.label: The Chant Hook
slots.purpose: FEEL: Anthemic and chant-able — the crowd-participation moment. TRICK: Layer a group-shouted gang-vocal on the hook line, panned wide, so it reads as call-and-response rather than a lead vocal.
slots.groove: Full sequencer plus a doubled bass layer; gang-shouted chant vocal panned wide across the stereo field.

slots.label: Loop Receding
slots.purpose: FEEL: The loop receding into the dark. TRICK: Let the sequencer keep running under a long fade rather than a hard stop — EBM tracks are DJ tools first, so they should be mixable out.
slots.groove: Sequencer loop continues under a long fade; percussion thins out gradually rather than cutting.
